headline: A premise-first audit finds limited selection signal, modest realized speedup, and compute-dependent render corruption in one world-action-model stack
summary: A preprint by Liu et al. audits test-time scaling on Cosmos Policy in RoboCasa. In that configuration, the authors report that their deployable value selector performed 1.66 percentage points below random selection; a hindsight oracle gained 1.40 points, with an episode-level interval spanning zero, while 82% of tested states had identical candidate outcomes. Token pruning removed up to 47.9% of per-forward FLOPs but delivered at most 1.152× measured end-to-end speedup on the deployed path (1.253× with future-image decoding excluded), below a pre-registered 1.5× target. A power gate halted the full adaptive-allocation experiment, so its effect remains unresolved. The authors also identify a silent OpenGL render corruption in the tested RoboCasa/robosuite stack, report a detector and fix, and find the corruption more frequent in a non-standard compute-heavy planning path; they say the official direct-policy benchmark is not materially affected. These are author-reported, configuration-specific findings, not evidence that test-time scaling generally fails.
